deep.reconstruction: Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages): Grothendieck studies systems of pseudolines in the real projective plane, drawn as discs with antipodal boundary identification. A 'relative position' L is a combinatorial isotopy type of such a system, here focused on a distinguished pair of pseudolines D, D'. To each L he attaches a characteristic polygon Delta_L, a disc whose boundary is cut into arcs. These are arcs of incidence: specialization arcs, generalization arcs and inertia arcs. Specialization corresponds to a degeneration in which a crossing of D, D' slides through another line (a triangle collapse, i.e. a Ringel mutation). Generalization is the inverse operation ('écraser les bras', antibalayage). The goal is a cellular surface whose cells are the polygons Delta_L. If a is a generalization arc of L and a' the corresponding specialization arc of L', one glues Delta_L to Delta_L' along a = a'. To fix the gluing one needs an identification of the 'orientation' objects omega(Delta_L) ≃ omega(L) and omega(Delta_L') ≃ omega(L'). He first uses the 'evident' (tautological) transport isomorphism, applied along the two antipodal generalization arcs (top-left and lower-left figures: three discs glued in a chain). On reflection he rejects it. The right identification is the opposite one: it exchanges the endpoints s and t of the arc, hence D with D'. This is the reflection in the axis (s,t)=a, 'the isomorphism of transport for the opposite orientation'. With this twisted gluing the large right-hand figure (four discs around a central dark curvilinear triangle, labels D0, D0', D1, D1', alpha, beta) shows a key property: all faces of the resulting complex have order 4. These faces are the cells dual to those cut out by the inertia arcs. Their vertices correspond to edges of the characteristic polygons. Their sides are of three types according to the transition arcs bounding them: specialization, generalization and mixed. The next page confirms that each square has one spec side, one gen side and two mixed sides. Faces correspond bijectively to pairs (L,a) with a an incidence arc of specialization type. The dual map is described as coming from the graph of relative positions (vertices = relative positions, edges = mutations) with 'semi-circularisation'. In modern terms he is building a 2-dimensional cell complex (a square complex/ribbon structure) on the flip graph of pseudoline-arrangement types, i.e. a 2-skeleton for the stratified space of arrangements. The next page admits the construction is incomplete because hypercritical positions have been left out.
errors: No outright error is visible. The choice of gluing isomorphism is explicitly revised mid-page: the 'evident' transport isomorphism is replaced by the s<->t swapping reflection. The first figures therefore illustrate a gluing he then abandons.

The construction is incomplete as stated: hypercritical relative positions and the arcs into/out of them are omitted. The next page acknowledges this, so the claim that all faces are of order 4 holds only for the partial complex.
Why the twisted identification is forced is not argued; it is asserted after looking at the figure.

ideas.what: Graph of combinatorial types (relative positions) of pseudoline systems with edges given by specialization/generalization (triangle-collapse) moves
ideas.modern_name: Mutation/flip graph of pseudoline arrangements (Ringel's theorem), higher Bruhat order B(n,2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Ringel (1956); Manin–Schechtman (1989); Ziegler, Felsner and others

ideas.what: Gluing characteristic polygons Delta_L along matching generalization/specialization arcs to get a cellular surface; choice of the gluing isomorphism of 'orientation' torsors omega (tautological vs. opposite/s<->t reflection)
ideas.modern_name: 2-dimensional CW/ribbon (map) structure on a stratified configuration space; gluing data via orientation torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart known; closest is cell structures on higher Bruhat orders and Salvetti-type complexes
ideas.where_published: Spirit close to the 'Teichmüller-Lego'/cellular decompositions in Esquisse d'un programme, but not this construction

ideas.what: With the twisted identification all faces are quadrilaterals, indexed by pairs (L,a), with sides of type spec, gen and mixed
ideas.modern_name: Square complex / commutation squares in a flip complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Square 2-cells (commuting moves) appear in higher Bruhat order and flip-complex literature (Manin–Schechtman, Ziegler)

ideas.what: Dual map derived from the graph of relative positions with 'semi-circularisation'
ideas.modern_name: Dual cell decomposition / ribbon graph from cyclic orderings at vertices
ideas.where_published: Maps and dessins in Esquisse d'un programme

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to build a cellular surface whose 2-cells are the characteristic polygons of relative positions of pseudolines, glued along mutation arcs. He finds that the correct gluing uses the orientation-reversing transport (swapping D and D'), making all dual faces squares. The construction is left incomplete (hypercritical positions omitted) and apparently never finished or published.
missed.quote: il me semble pas ... la bonne l'isom d'identification qu'il faudrait plutôt ... c'est que transforme s en t, t en s ... Par cette identification toutes les "faces" sont d'ordre 4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical surface/2-complex built on the flip graph of pseudoline-arrangement types bears on the topology of realization spaces and stratified spaces of arrangements. It would sit alongside higher Bruhat orders and the cellular structures in Manin–Schechtman, Ziegler and Felsner. The explicit square-face structure with typed sides (spec/gen/mixed) and the torsor-twisted gluing rule do not appear in that literature as such.

missed.claim: The page links pseudoline combinatorics (oriented matroids of rank 3) to Grothendieck's cartographic/ribbon-graph viewpoint. Moduli-type spaces are obtained by gluing polygons along boundary arcs with explicit transport isomorphisms, as in the Teichmüller tower/Lego program.
missed.quote: les sommets de la carte duale ... des graphes des positions relatives, avec la semi-circularisation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests treating spaces of pseudoline arrangements with the same 'map/dessin' methods Grothendieck proposed for moduli of curves. That bridge has been little explored.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuinely unpublished construction: a cellular surface on the space of relative positions of pseudolines, with a non-obvious twisted gluing rule yielding square faces. But it is a work-in-progress fragment, admitted incomplete, and the general theme (flip graphs, square commutation cells) is known from later literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 is likely 'qui explique le recollement de l'un des cas, ou l'unique recollement de l'autre', not 'recatement ... on l'unique'.
'cas de généralisation antipodiques' is likely 'arcs de généralisation antipodiques'.
'le cas Bien de transport' is likely 'l'isom. de transport'.
'de façon imaginée' is likely 'de façon imagée'; also 'faire la symétrie par rapport à l'axe (s,t)=a'.
Right column: 'et les sommets de la carte duale de cette décomposition (?) des graphes des positions relatives', not 'cartes duales de cette déduite'.

'Les cours obtenus ici comme faces ... des cours fermés par les cas d'inertie ... "cours caractéristiques"' should probably read 'carrés' (or 'cercles') and 'arcs d'inertie'. The next page speaks of 'le carré'.
